messages:
alex: Quick thought: provide a single SDK abstraction that surfaces either paged HTTP or a long-lived gRPC stream as an iterator. Goal: reduce boilerplate for simple consumers while keeping explicit options for Go.

maya: makes sense. Are we prioritizing latency, developer ergonomics, or server load? each affects how aggressive the stream mode should be.

alex: mostly latency and fewer TCP/HTTP handshakes for large result sets. Also cleaner for async consumers in TS/Python.

sergio: main hazard is resume semantics. Streams can drop. If we want resume, server must emit periodic opaque resume tokens. Otherwise clients will have inconsistent reads.

lee: agreed. From Go's perspective we should not hide the transport. Expose Pages() and Stream() explicitly, and maybe Provide Iter() that picks best-effort behavior for high-level users.

alex: API sketch:
Python:
```py
# best-effort iterator that prefers stream when available
for item in client.items.iter(parent='p/1', prefer_stream=True):
    handle(item)

# explicit APIs
for page in client.items.pages(parent='p/1'):
  for item in page.items: ...

stream = client.items.stream(parent='p/1')
async for item in stream: ...
```
TS sketch:
```ts
// async iterator prefers stream
for await (const it of client.items.iter({ parent: 'p/1', preferStream: true })) {
  // items
}
```

sergio: resume rules proposal:
- server includes `x-resume-token: <opaque>` every K items (K configurable).
- client tracks last token; on stream failure, client can request pages starting from resume token.
- tokens remain opaque; server may include debug suffix in logs (not in header).

maya: what about ordering? we should state that streams do NOT guarantee strict global ordering across shards. Consumers must not rely on order unless documented.

lee: backpressure: streaming must provide a bounded client buffer. If consumer is slow, SDK should apply TCP/window backpressure or drop into synchronous mode. We should expose `stream_buffer_size` and `batch_callback` options.

alex: retries: try to reconnect the stream with exponential backoff up to N attempts (default 3). On final failure, fallback to paged reads starting from last resume token.

sergio: auth rotation: long-lived streams can outlive tokens. SDK should attempt a transparent reauth and resume. If reauth fails, fall back. Document this clearly.

maya: metrics/billing: streaming can't hide per-item accounting. server must emit item counts and we should map them to billing events. recommend `x-stream-progress: <count>` and a server-side event stream for billing hooks.

alex: config proposal: `prefer_streaming` (bool), `stream_checkpoint_interval` (int), `stream_retries` (int), `stream_buffer` (int), `stream_reconnect_backoff_ms` (list). Keep defaults conservative.

lee: Go SDK ergonomics: explicit `Stream(ctx, opts)` returning `(<-chan Item, CancelFunc)` or an iterator with `Next(ctx) (Item, error)`. Avoid hidden goroutines that swallow context cancellations.

sergio: tests: simulate mid-stream disconnects and assert that items are not duplicated/missing when fallback occurs; verify auth refresh paths; verify memory under slow consumers; verify resume token correctness across server versions.

maya: rollout plan: feature flag the streaming endpoint, enable internal teams first, measure failure rate, resume success rate, and billing parity. Only flip prefer_streaming default after stable metrics.

alex: canary + SDK migration plan: SDKs default to `prefer_streaming=false` initially; advanced users can opt-in. After 2+ weeks of stable metrics we change default in minor release.

lee: minor UX idea: add `iter.meta()` or `stream.meta()` to surface last_resume_token and items_read so long-running consumers can checkpoint.

sergio: one more: make resume token format versioned (opaque but short prefix) so we can evolve server-side semantics without breaking older SDKs.

ci-bot: noted CI/bench requirement: add e2e tests for stream fallback + microbenchmark for latency and CPU/memory under different consumer speeds.

alex: next steps: maya will author RFC follow-up with API sketches and test matrices; lee will write Go signature proposals; sergio will detail server-side headers/events; i'll prototype a minimal server stream that emits resume tokens every 50 items.

maya: will tag @engineering-leads and schedule a short sync to align on rollouts.

lee: sgtm. thanks all.
